title: Finiteness of higher direct images of finite-type morphisms
statement:
Let $u:X\to Y$ be a
finite-type morphism
between finite-type schemes over a field, and let $F$ be a finite
constructible
sheaf with prime-to-characteristic
coefficients $\Lambda$.
Then $Ru_*F$ is bounded
constructible. If $u$ is separated, so is
$Ru_!F$. If its geometric
fibres have dimension at most $d$, the latter satisfies
$R^qu_!F=0$ for $q>2d$.

proof.text: Use the finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]: it is annihilated by a positive integer $N$ invertible in the base field $k$, and hence on every scheme over $k$. Put $K=F[0]$ in the ordinary etale derived category. Its only nonzero cohomology sheaf is $\mathcal H^0(K)=F$, so $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Apply [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] to $u$ and $K$. Its hypotheses are precisely finite-type schemes over the field $k$ and the stated allowable finite coefficients; it imposes no separatedness hypothesis. It gives $Ru_*F\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, proving the first assertion.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: the ordinary direct-image assertion, including the nonseparated case

proof.text: For the remaining assertions suppose $u$ is separated. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian; in particular $Y$ is quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to the separated finite-type $u$. By [def-nagata-compactification] its compactification is $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$, where $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, $r$ is proper, and $rj=u$. The properness definition [def-weil-proper-morphism] includes finite type. To check that $\overline X$ is of finite type over $k$, use [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: take a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $Y$ with each $R_i$ finitely generated over $k$, then a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_{ia}$ of $r^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R_i)$ with $B_{ia}$ finitely generated over $R_i$. The images of the finite generators of $R_i$ together with the generators of $B_{ia}$ generate $B_{ia}$ over $k$. These finitely many affines cover $\overline X$, giving the required finite-type structure. The same Noetherian lemma makes $\overline X$ Noetherian. For each of $X$, $Y$ and $\overline X$, local Noetherianity gives an affine neighbourhood with Noetherian coordinate ring at every point, and quasi-compactness selects finitely many of these neighbourhoods. Thus these schemes satisfy exactly the finite-Noetherian-affine-cover convention in the compact-support definition and comparison statement used in step 4. No dimension bound on $\overline X$ or on the fibres of $r$ has been imposed.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: choose the Nagata compactification; explicit checks of its hypotheses

proof.text: By [lem-fin-extension-by-zero], applied to the open immersion $j$ between the finite-type $k$-schemes just obtained, the sheaf $j_!F$ is constructible on $\overline X_{\mathrm{et}}$. As a complex in degree zero it is bounded constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Apply [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] to the proper map $r:\overline X\to Y$ and this complex, with the same finite coefficients. It follows that $Rr_*(j_!F[0])\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$. This uses bounded constructibility for proper direct image without any specified fibre-dimension bound.

source.place: Proof, middle sentences: extension by zero is constructible and proper direct image is bounded constructible

proof.text: The chosen-compactification definition [def-amb-etale-compact-support] sends $F[0]$ to $Rr_*Dj_!(F[0])$. The normalization $Dj_!Q_X\cong Q_{\overline X}j_!$ in that definition gives $Dj_!(F[0])\cong (j_!F)[0]$: degreewise extension by zero sends the sole possibly nonzero term $F$ in degree zero to $j_!F$ in degree zero, and sends every zero term and differential to zero. All inputs here are bounded below. The comparison statement [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] applies to this compactifiable separated finite-type map of Noetherian schemes with finite commutative coefficients, and identifies the chosen candidate with the compactification-independent $Ru_!F$. Consequently $Ru_!F\cong Rr_*(j_!F[0])$ is bounded constructible by step 3: an isomorphism induces isomorphisms on cohomology sheaves and hence preserves their vanishing and finite lisse stratifications. This supplies the compact-support assertion in the same ordinary etale category as the first assertion.

source.place: Proof, formula Ru_! = Rr_* j_!: distinguish the chosen candidate from the comparison-independent functor

proof.text: Now assume the geometric fibres of the original map $u$ have dimension at most $d$. The finite ring $\Lambda$ has positive additive exponent $m$ dividing the annihilating integer $N$ from step 1. Indeed, let $m$ be the additive order of $1_\Lambda$. Then $N\cdot 1_\Lambda=0$ implies $m\mid N$. For every $a\in\Lambda$, $ma=(m1_\Lambda)a=0$, whereas any integer annihilating the additive group annihilates $1_\Lambda$ and is divisible by $m$. Hence $m$ is exactly the additive exponent (also $m=1$ for the zero ring). Thus $m$ is invertible on $Y$: writing $N=mt$, if $N$ is a unit then $tN^{-1}$ is an inverse for $m$. Apply [lem-dg-compact-support-amplitude] to $u$, $A=\Lambda$ and the sheaf $F$. This statement allows every etale $A$-module sheaf, so it applies in particular to this finite constructible one, and gives $R^qu_!F=0$ for every $q>2d$. The dimensional hypothesis in this application is on $u$ itself. The proof therefore never requires a dimension bound for the compactification map $r$.

source.place: Proof, final sentences: apply the sharp compact-support amplitude bound to the original fibres
